text.p: These are the leading stories in Serbian and Montenegrin press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
-- SERBIA --
POLITIKA
- The Serbian government has proposed new rules for municipal elections.
- The Serbian Academy of Science and Arts will sue Jacques Delors because of his statement to the French TV in which he accused the academy for being the main culprit for ethnic cleansing.

- Croatian prisons still hold 117 persons from Yugoslavia, Bosnian Serb Republic and Krajina in Croatia, secretary of the Yugoslav government commission for humanitarian issues and missing persons Maksim Korac said after two-day talks between Yugoslav and Croatian government commissions.
- Serbian construction minister Branislav Ivkovic and Palestinian housing minister Abd al-Rahman Hamad signed an agreement on cooperation on reconstruction and development of Palestinian territories.
- Acting general manager of Beogradska Banka said all 20 members of Beogradska Banka will form a banking giant BB-group on Thursday.
NASA BORBA
- New U.S. diplomatic affensive in Balkans. U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright to visit Bosnia, maybe Belgrade and Zagreb.
- Hundreds of thousands of German marks taken from foreigners by the Yugoslav customs at Yugoslav borders have vanished.
- Serbia's health workers' strike to go on until all demands are met.
- International community objects to customs regulations envisaged by the agreement between Bosnian Serb Republic and Yugoslavia.
- The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia forms economic council.
-- MONTENEGRO --
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin President Momir Bulatovic said that the issue of common state (Yugoslavia) is the most important political issue in the Democratic Party of Socialists and the republic.

- Montenegrin vessel Lovcen released form sanctions regime will leave the port of New York on May 23. Other four Montenegrin ships blocked in various U.S. ports will start their journey home by June 1. New Orleans port authorities offered Montenegrin shipping company Jugooceanija to resume the line between U.S. and Mediterranean ports including Montenegro.
- Republic's parliament adopted territorial development plan by the year 2000.
- Republic's pension fund will pay out 60 percent instalment of April pensions with 54.3 million dinars. The maximum pension is 1,978 dinars while minimum is 523 dinars.
- Podgorica and Niksic surgeons demand resignation of Montenegrin health minister Miomir Mugosa. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
